text:
kai: Heads-up, hitting a weird HF->Redwood chat_template conversion bug while onboarding xglm-chat-6B. System role ends up at the end of the prompt and there's an unexpected <s> token injected between role separators. Outputs repeat the first assistant token a lot.

kai: Minimal repro below (original Jinja-style chat_template we got from HF model card):
```jinja
{%- for m in messages -%}
{% if m.role == 'system' -%}
<<SYS>>
{{ m.content }}
<</SYS>>

{%- else -%}
{{ m.role }}: {{ m.content }}

{%- endif -%}
{%- endfor -%}
```

kai: And this is what our conversion script produced for Redwood prompt (string concat) — note system content ends up after assistant blocks and we see an extra <s> token where we expected a newline: 
```text
user: Hello
assistant: Hi! How can I help?
<s>
system: You are a helpful assistant that replies in short sentences.
```

dave: Hmm that <s> looks like a tokenizer special token rather than something from the template. Did we accidentally call tokenizer.encode on the whole reconstructed prompt instead of encoding messages separately? Also did we check tokenizer.bos_token_id vs model.config.bos_token_id?

maria: Quick checks I ran: some HF tokenizers (esp. from transformers with fast tokenizers) will add a leading <s> or space if you call tokenizer.encode_plus(..., add_special_tokens=True) on sub-pieces. If the conversion concatenates fragments then run encode once, you can get an extra BOS in the middle. Try encoding each message and then concatenating ids (without adding special tokens for the inner pieces).

kai: Ah good call. Our conversion pipeline currently does: 
```python
pieces = [render(message) for message in messages]
ids = tokenizer.encode("\n".join(pieces), add_special_tokens=True)
```
so that will add a bos at the very start, but why is it showing up mid-prompt?

eva: One possibility: messages is a list-like but in our code path we convert to a set for dedupe at one point (bug). Sets are unordered; if system got moved to end, then you encoded and the BOS belongs to the new first element (which used to be a different message). Also if you later re-insert markers like "system:" as plain text, they might be tokenized into tokens that collide with special token ids depending on tokenizer normalization.

dave: Also check tokenizer.special_tokens_map and tokenizer.all_special_tokens. Some tokenizers map '<s>' to BOS; if you are joining with '
' and not stripping, the string "
<s>
" could be tokenized into separate tokens that include the special token again.

maria: Another practical quick fix: when building the Redwood prompt, enforce order explicitly — system first, then alternating user/assistant — don't rely on the incoming list order unless you validated it. And when calling the tokenizer, do per-message encode with add_special_tokens=False, then add the model's BOS/EOS once at the end with tokenizer.build_inputs_with_special_tokens or manual insertion using tokenizer.bos_token_id.

kai: Good. I'll change conversion to use deterministic ordering and per-message encodes. One more weirdness: when we test outputs between fp16 and 4-bit quantized, the quantized run seems to hallucinate an extra "Assistant:" token at the start. Could that be tied to the BOS mapping difference?

eva: Yes — quantized runtimes often reuse token ids differently if you accidentally remap the vocabulary or pass token ids that include special tokens in unexpected positions. Also some conversion tools (we use a small C++ kernel for tokenization in the runtime) expect raw token ids and will treat id==bos_id specially. If you feed them a token sequence with a BOS id in the middle they might interpret that as restart and re-output a role label.

dave: For debugging: 1) print tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(ids) for the exact ids you send to the model in both float16 and quant runs; 2) compare model.config.bos_token_id and tokenizer.bos_token_id; 3) run with skip_special_tokens=True on decode to confirm what the tokenizer thinks is special.

maria: Also check the model card/config.json from HF — sometimes chat models add custom special tokens (like '<|system|>') and set tokenizer.add_prefix_space or do unicode normalization; we had a case where config.json listed 'sep_token' that the tokenizer ignored since it wasn't in the vocab, causing a different tokenization path.

kai: I'll open a small repro and attach the failing prompt + both token id sequences and run a tiny eval comparing outputs (LM-bleu/ROUGE-ish and a token-level diff) between float16 and 4-bit. If it's a conversion bug we can patch conversion script and re-run quantized tests.

eva: SG — if you put the repro in a gist, I can run a quick local loop with the runtime and the quantized backend. Also add a minimal test in model-onboarding checks: assert system_is_first(messages) and assert no_mid_bos(ids).

ci-bot: Created issue #4521: "chat-template conversion: unexpected mid-prompt BOS and role-order variance" (assigned to kai) :white_check_mark:

kai: Thanks — I'll iterate on the conversion and ping y'all once I have the token diffs. :thumbsup:
